title: Never Cut a Rule in Half
briefMd:
# Phase 3 · Never Cut a Rule in Half

The travel and expense rules are written one rule per sentence, and each rule is long: a condition and a limit, 140 to 220 characters ("Hotel rooms are booked by the travel desk at least ten days before arrival, and a room may cost up to 160 euros a night in capital cities and 120 euros a night elsewhere."). Half a rule is a wrong answer, so a question counts only when the whole rule sits in one retrieved chunk.

You control **chunk size** (characters) and **split strategy**. There is no overlap here. Retrieval is BM25, top 5 chunks, and all five go into the context.

Fixed windows cut wherever the character count runs out. Bigger windows cut fewer rules, but five of them cost too many tokens.

**Gates:** recall@5 ≥ 0.90 and mean context tokens (top-5 chunks) ≤ 180 on the hidden set.
